mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the past 60 days reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 60 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite high FEDFUNDS levels.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog but proxy via HOUST for industrial demand) predicts higher future corporate profits and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 60-day moving average baseline by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average during a period of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) suggests supply-side constraints that weigh on equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0% while INDPRO is below its 50-week MA
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the described supply conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 3%, it indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers real discount rates, encouraging firms to invest in long-term projects that expand equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no outperformance relative to a 60-day risk-free rate proxy (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (not directly observable) inferred through a sharp decline in PAYEMS accompanied by a rise in UNRATE suggests labor market cooling that reduces consumer spending momentum and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by > 5,000 jobs while UNRATE increases by > 0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) when labor conditions deteriorate as described.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indices (CPIAUCSL) above 4% trigger expectations of future wage growth, which elevates inflation-linked equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat (p > 0.05) despite CPIAUCSL in high-inflation territory.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side loose policy (indicated by FEDFUNDS < 3%) combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a dislocation where capacity utilization falls but demand remains steady, creating temporary equity market volatility that results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 3% while INDPRO decreases by > 2% from the prior quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show consistent outperformance over a risk-free benchmark (p < 0.05) contrary to the mechanism's prediction.
